title: Review-convergence-v8
notes:
Efficiency: no findings. Secretx fetch is async once at startup; bcrypt dummy hash is precomputed once. No hot-path issues introduced.
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — One real cross-service consistency gap (secretx URI not validated at config time for imap, where reader validates eagerly). The typing erasure in imap's build_credential_store is a pattern debt that grows if error variants are added. Test coverage gap for the new dispatch logic is the most actionable near-term item.
Confidence: 10% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: t4xr.1 (the missing validation is a real inconsistency but the runtime error message is clear enough that it may not be worth fixing). Uncertainty driven by: did not inspect the full secretx crate API to confirm from_uri() is cheap enough to call at validate() time. Would raise confidence if: ran the imap test suite with a bad secretx URI to confirm error surfacing.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — No unsafe, no unwrap in production paths, no clippy-level issues introduced. The main Rust idiom gap is that imap build_credential_store uses a flat-string error type where reader uses a typed enum with thiserror. This is a consistency issue, not an unsoundness.
